newsitem.title: USA: CNET shares off after Web service detailed.
newsitem.headline: CNET shares off after Web service detailed.

text.p: Shares of CNET Inc slid on Monday after the company revealed further details of a advertising-supported Web service it plans to start in September, analysts said.

Robertson Stephens analyst Keith Benjamin said the new Snap! Online service could eventually compete with service provided by online media companies such as America Online Inc, Compuserve Corp., Yahoo Inc and Excite Inc.

But the analyst said he was pushing out his break-even point for CNET to the third quarter of 1998 from the fourth quarter of this year based on the costs of building up a staff for the new online service.
Shares of CNET were down 3-1/4 at 28 early Monday afternoon.

Benjamin now expects 1997 losses for the Internet news and television production company to be $1 a share, wider than his earlier estimate of $0.70. He expects a profit of $0.05 a share next year, compared with his previous profit estimate of $0.15.

The analyst said the strategy of distributing Snap! Online through Internet service providers (ISPs) and personal computer makers, who pay annual licence fees to CNET, could provide significant advertising and commerce revenues from 1999 and beyond.

"I think it's going to work out for CNET that they can create some siginficant value," he said. "By the December quarter or the beginning of next year it's possible that we'll see significant numbers of subscribers."

Separately, Alex. Brown said it lowered its rating on shares of Yahoo! Inc to buy from strong buy. The stock, which closed Friday just shy of its trading high, was off 2-5/8 at 36-5/8 Monday afternoon.
Shares of AOL were down one at 58-3/4, Compuserve was unchanged at 10-5/8 and Excite dropped 13/16 to 13-3/8.
